import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dirac–Motzkin conjecture

Let $P$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, not all on one line.
An *ordinary line* of $P$ is a line containing exactly two points of $P$. The Sylvester–Gallai
theorem says that $P$ has at least one ordinary line. The Dirac–Motzkin conjecture asks for the
minimum number $t_2(n)$ of ordinary lines: it states that $P$ always determines at least
$\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ ordinary lines.

The bound is attained for every even $n > 4$ by a construction of Böröczky, and for $n = 7$
(Kelly–Moser) and $n = 13$ (McKee). Green and Tao proved that the number of ordinary lines is at
least $n/2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sylvester–Gallai theorem, The number of ordinary lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvester%E2%80%93Gallai_theorem%23The_number_of_ordinary_lines)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [GT13] Green, B., Tao, T., *On sets defining few ordinary lines*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 50
  (2013), 409–468. [arXiv:1208.4714](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.4714)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace DiracMotzkinConjecture

/--
The set of *ordinary lines* determined by a finite set `P` of points in the plane: the lines
through two distinct points of `P` that contain exactly two points of `P`. Lines are represented
as affine subspaces of `ℝ²`.
-/
def ordinaryLines (P : Finset ℝ²) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) :=
  {L | ∃ p ∈ P, ∃ q ∈ P, p ≠ q ∧ L = line[ℝ, p, q] ∧ ((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ P).ncard = 2}

/-- The empty set determines no ordinary lines. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem ordinaryLines_empty : ordinaryLines ∅ = ∅ := by
  simp [ordinaryLines]

/-- Two distinct points determine exactly one ordinary line, namely the line through them. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem ordinaryLines_pair {p q : ℝ²} (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    ordinaryLines {p, q} = {line[ℝ, p, q]} := by
  ext L
  simp only [ordinaryLines, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton,
    Finset.coe_pair, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab, rfl, -⟩
    rcases ha with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hb with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hab
    · rfl
    · rw [Set.pair_comm]
    · exact absurd rfl hab
  · rintro rfl
    refine ⟨p, Or.inl rfl, q, Or.inr rfl, hpq, rfl, ?_⟩
    rw [Set.inter_eq_right.mpr, Set.ncard_pair hpq]
    exact Set.insert_subset (left_mem_affineSpan_pair ℝ p q)
      (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr (right_mem_affineSpan_pair ℝ p q))

/--
**Dirac–Motzkin conjecture.**
Every finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, not all on one line,
determines at least $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ ordinary lines, that is, lines containing exactly two
of the points.

The hypothesis that the points are not all collinear is essential: a collinear set has no
ordinary lines. It also forces $n \geq 3$. The floor is needed: the Kelly–Moser configuration
($n = 7$, $3$ ordinary lines) and the McKee configuration ($n = 13$, $6$ ordinary lines) attain
$\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ ordinary lines. Natural number division `P.card / 2` is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture (P : Finset ℝ²) (hP : ¬ Collinear ℝ (P : Set ℝ²)) :
    P.card / 2 ≤ (ordinaryLines P).ncard := by
  sorry

/--
Green and Tao [GT13] proved that there is an absolute constant $n_0$ such that every set of
$n \geq n_0$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, not all on one line, determines at least $n/2$ ordinary
lines. The inequality $n/2 \leq N$ is written as $n \leq 2N$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 52]
theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture.variants.green_tao :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset ℝ², n₀ ≤ P.card → ¬ Collinear ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) →
      P.card ≤ 2 * (ordinaryLines P).ncard := by
  sorry

end DiracMotzkinConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (floor, non-collinearity hypothesis, distinction from Green–Tao's n/2 form) match the Wikipedia article and the Green–Tao paper.
modeling_decisions: The list-page statement is terse; the precise formulation was taken from the Wikipedia article section 'The number of ordinary lines' (Dirac 1951: t₂(n) ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ for all n), as the decomposition notes prescribe, not from Green–Tao's 'n/2 for n ≥ n₀' form.

Points are modelled as a `Finset ℝ²` where `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (the repo's scoped notation), so n = P.card. This is the Euclidean plane; the projective plane is not used (the article notes the two settings are combinatorially equivalent for finite sets).

'Not all collinear' is `¬ Collinear ℝ (P : Set ℝ²)` (Mathlib: rank of vectorSpan ≤ 1). Since ∅, singletons and pairs are collinear, this hypothesis automatically forces n ≥ 3; no separate n ≥ 3 hypothesis is added.

Ordinary lines are represented as affine subspaces `line[ℝ, p, q]` for distinct p, q ∈ P with `((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ ↑P).ncard = 2`. Every line containing exactly two points of P is the affine span of those two points, so this set is exactly the set of ordinary lines; it is finite (image of pairs), so `Set.ncard` is the genuine cardinality (no ncard-of-infinite-set = 0 issue).
⌊n/2⌋ is written as ℕ-division `P.card / 2`, so the Kelly–Moser (n = 7, 3 lines) and McKee (n = 13, 6 lines) configurations attain equality rather than violate the statement.

An extra `research solved` variant `dirac_motzkin_conjecture.variants.green_tao` records the Green–Tao theorem (∃ n₀, every non-collinear P with n₀ ≤ |P| has |P| ≤ 2·#ordinaryLines, i.e. at least n/2 ordinary lines) exactly as stated in arXiv:1208.4714 Theorem 1.1; n/2 ≤ N is encoded as n ≤ 2N to stay in ℕ.
AMS tags 51 (Geometry) and 52 (Convex and discrete geometry) chosen to match the tags 'geometry, discrete geometry'.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Erdős 101 has a `private` `linesWithPointsFor k S` (lines spanned by pairs of S with exactly k points of S) — private, so not reusable; `EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear`/`NonCollinearFor` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean only forbid collinear tuples and cannot count lines; Mathlib's `Collinear`, `affineSpan`/`line[ℝ, p, q]` and `Set.ncard` are used as building blocks.
new_definitions.name: DiracMotzkinConjecture.ordinaryLines
new_definitions.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of 'ordinary line' (a line containing exactly two points of a given finite set) or of 'the lines determined by a point set'. The definition is problem-specific, so it lives in the problem file (as CONTRIBUTING/STATEMENTS allow) with two `category test` API lemmas (`ordinaryLines_empty`, `ordinaryLines_pair`) proved in the file.

dirac_motzkin_conjecture.why: Stated as: for every P : Finset ℝ² with ¬ Collinear ℝ ↑P, P.card / 2 ≤ (ordinaryLines P).ncard, where ordinaryLines P is the set of affine lines line[ℝ, p, q] (p ≠ q in P) meeting P in exactly two points. ℕ-division gives the floor ⌊n/2⌋ required by the article; the non-collinearity hypothesis excludes the degenerate case and forces n ≥ 3.

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace DiracMotzkinConjecture

open scoped Classical in
/--
**Dirac–Motzkin conjecture.** Every set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane that is
not collinear spans at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ ordinary lines, where an ordinary
line is a line containing exactly two points of the set.

Here distinct pairs of points determine affine lines. The `Finset.image` ensures that
each such line is counted only once. The non-collinearity hypothesis excludes the
degenerate case of all points lying on one line (and in particular forces $n \geq 3$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture (n : ℕ) (S : Finset ℝ²) (hcard : S.card = n)
    (hnc : ¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)) :
    n / 2 ≤
      ((S.offDiag.filter fun p : ℝ² × ℝ² =>
          (S.filter fun x => x ∈ affineSpan ℝ ({p.1, p.2} : Set ℝ²)).card = 2).image
        fun p => affineSpan ℝ ({p.1, p.2} : Set ℝ²)).card := by
  sorry

end DiracMotzkinConjecture
modeling_decisions: The terse list-page entry was made precise using the supplied Wikipedia article: for every finite non-collinear set of n points in ℝ², the number of ordinary lines is at least ⌊n/2⌋.
A finite configuration is represented by `S : Finset ℝ²` together with `S.card = n`; thus points are distinct and the quantification is over all finite n-point sets.
A line determined by distinct points `p.1` and `p.2` is represented by `affineSpan ℝ {p.1, p.2}`. Pairs come from `S.offDiag`, ensuring distinct endpoints and hence a genuine line.

An ordinary line is selected by requiring exactly two points of `S` to belong to that affine span. `Finset.image` over affine subspaces identifies the two pair orientations and all other duplicate descriptions, so its cardinality is the number of distinct ordinary lines.
The lower bound `n / 2` uses natural-number division and therefore represents `⌊n/2⌋`, including the essential odd-n cases.
Non-collinearity is expressed as `¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)`. No separate `3 ≤ n` hypothesis is imposed because it follows from non-collinearity and adding it would be redundant.

  sorry

The ordinary lines form a `Set` of affine subspaces, so `Set.ncard` counts distinct geometric lines and does not double-count ordered pairs or multiple pairs spanning the same line.

open EuclideanGeometry

plane that is not collinear determines at least $\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor$ ordinary lines. Here,
an ordinary line contains exactly two points of $S$, and lines determined by different pairs

theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture (S : Set ℝ²) (hS : S.Finite) (hS' : ¬ Collinear ℝ S) :

        p ≠ q ∧ L = affineSpan ℝ {p, q} ∧ (↑L ∩ S).ncard = 2}
    S.ncard / 2 ≤ ordinaryLines.ncard := by
  sorry

end DiracMotzkinConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Dirac–Motzkin conjecture

Let $S$ be a finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, not all on one line. A line is
*ordinary* for $S$ if it contains exactly two points of $S$. The Sylvester–Gallai theorem says
that $S$ spans at least one ordinary line. Let $t_2(n)$ be the minimum number of ordinary lines
spanned by a set of $n$ points, not all on one line.

The **Dirac–Motzkin conjecture** states that $t_2(n) \geq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ for all $n$.
The floor is essential: the Kelly–Moser configuration ($n = 7$, three ordinary lines) and the
McKee configuration ($n = 13$, six ordinary lines) attain the bound $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
Green and Tao proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $n$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Sylvester–Gallai theorem, The number of ordinary lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvester%E2%80%93Gallai_theorem%23The_number_of_ordinary_lines)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [GT13] Green, B., Tao, T., *On sets defining few ordinary lines*, Discrete Comput. Geom. 50
  (2013), 409–468. [arXiv:1208.4714](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.4714)
- [KM58] Kelly, L. M., Moser, W. O. J., *On the number of ordinary lines determined by $n$
  points*, Canad. J. Math. 10 (1958), 210–219.
- [CS93] Csima, J., Sawyer, E. T., *There exist $6n/13$ ordinary points*, Discrete Comput.
  Geom. 9 (1993), 187–202.
-/

namespace DiracMotzkinConjecture

open EuclideanGeometry

/-- The set of *ordinary lines* of a finite set `S` of points in the Euclidean plane `ℝ²`:
the lines through two distinct points of `S` that contain exactly two points of `S`. -/
noncomputable def ordinaryLines (S : Finset ℝ²) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) :=
  {L | ∃ p ∈ S, ∃ q ∈ S, p ≠ q ∧ L = line[ℝ, p, q] ∧ ((L : Set ℝ²) ∩ S).ncard = 2}

/-- A finite set of points spans only finitely many ordinary lines. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem ordinaryLines_finite (S : Finset ℝ²) : (ordinaryLines S).Finite := by
  refine ((S ×ˢ S).finite_toSet.image fun pq : ℝ² × ℝ² => line[ℝ, pq.1, pq.2]).subset ?_
  rintro L ⟨p, hp, q, hq, -, rfl, -⟩
  exact ⟨(p, q), by simpa using ⟨hp, hq⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The empty set spans no ordinary line. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem ordinaryLines_empty : ordinaryLines ∅ = ∅ := by
  ext L
  simp [ordinaryLines]

/-- A set of at least three collinear points spans no ordinary line. This is the degenerate
case excluded by the hypothesis of the Dirac–Motzkin conjecture. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem ordinaryLines_eq_empty_of_collinear (S : Finset ℝ²) (hS : Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²))
    (hcard : 3 ≤ S.card) : ordinaryLines S = ∅ := by
  ext L
  simp only [ordinaryLines, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨p, hp, q, hq, hpq, rfl, h2⟩
  have hsub : (S : Set ℝ²) ⊆ (line[ℝ, p, q] : Set ℝ²) := fun r hr =>
    hS.mem_affineSpan_of_mem_of_ne hp hq hr hpq
  rw [Set.inter_eq_right.mpr hsub, Set.ncard_coe_finset] at h2
  omega

/-- **Dirac–Motzkin conjecture.**
Every finite set $S$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, not all on one line, spans at least
$\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ ordinary lines, that is, lines containing exactly two points of $S$.
Here `S.card / 2` is natural number division, so it equals $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
The hypothesis that the points are not all collinear excludes the degenerate case of a
collinear set, which spans no ordinary line; it forces $n \geq 3$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture (S : Finset ℝ²) (hS : ¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)) :
    S.card / 2 ≤ (ordinaryLines S).ncard := by
  sorry

/-- Kelly and Moser [KM58] proved that every finite set of $n$ points in the plane, not all on
one line, spans at least $3n/7$ ordinary lines. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 52]
theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture.variants.kelly_moser (S : Finset ℝ²)
    (hS : ¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)) :
    3 * S.card ≤ 7 * (ordinaryLines S).ncard := by
  sorry

/-- Csima and Sawyer [CS93] proved that every finite set of $n \neq 7$ points in the plane, not
all on one line, spans at least $\lceil 6n/13 \rceil$ ordinary lines. The case $n = 7$ must be
excluded because of the Kelly–Moser configuration, which spans only three ordinary lines. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 52]
theorem dirac_motzkin_conjecture.variants.csima_sawyer (S : Finset ℝ²)
    (hS : ¬ Collinear ℝ (S : Set ℝ²)) (h7 : S.card ≠ 7) :
    6 * S.card ≤ 13 * (ordinaryLines S).ncard := by
  sorry

/-- Green and Tao [GT13, Theorem 1.2] proved the Dirac–Motzkin conjecture for all sufficiently
large $n$, in the stronger form: there is $n_0$ such that every set of $n \geq n_0$ points in
the plane, not all on one line, spans at least $n/2$ ordinary lines. -/

      n / 2 ≤ {L : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ² |
        Module.finrank ℝ L.direction = 1 ∧ (S ∩ (L : Set ℝ²)).ncard = 2}.ncard := by
  sorry
